summary: Explains how to control network connection and command timeouts, settable as playbook vars, environment variables, or ansible.cfg settings. Example sets the command timeout to 30 via `ansible_command_timeout`, `ANSIBLE_PERSISTENT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT`, or `[persistent_connection] command_timeout`.
questions: My network command times out, how do I give it longer?
How do I set the command timeout for one task on a Cisco device?
What's the environment variable for persistent command timeout?
How do I set network timeouts globally in ansible.cfg?

answer_card.title: Set network timeout options
answer_card.answer_md:
Timeouts can be set three ways (here, a 30 second command timeout):

Per task, as vars:
```yaml
- name: save running-config
  cisco.ios.ios_command:
    commands: copy running-config startup-config
  vars:
    ansible_command_timeout: 30
```
Environment variable:
```bash
export ANSIBLE_PERSISTENT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT=30
```
Globally in `ansible.cfg`:
```ini
[persistent_connection]
command_timeout = 30
```
Variable precedence determines which applies when several are set.
